name: gardner in rounds scored
description: Martin Gardner's 5x5 minichess played in rounds: both players move at once. Each round each player chooses one move in secret, and both moves are revealed and made together. There is no check: the king is simply captured, and the side that loses its king loses. Only two pieces moving onto the same square collide, and then both are removed. A piece that moves onto a square its target has just left lands there if it could move to an empty square, so two pieces that try to take each other in the same round trade places unharmed; a pawn's diagonal capture, which cannot land on an empty square, misses and the pawn stays. Two such misses at each other two rounds in a row bar that pair of captures until either square changes. If both kings fall in the same round, the side with more material left wins (queen 9, rook 5, bishop and knight 3, pawn 1) and equal material is a draw; the same count settles a game that reaches the move limit or the no-progress clock. A round counts as two moves on the clocks. This rule alone does not stop the kings' chase: a side behind in material will no longer trade both kings, so its king runs instead, and most games are still drawn by repetition.

provenance.preview: A preview: a new kind of game in which both players move at once, still being tested. Play it against the computer for practice; it is on no leaderboard yet, and its score is a first reading, not yet trusted.
